steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dark adaptation takes 20–30 minutes; avoid white light — use red light to preserve night vision

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Averted vision (looking slightly to the side) uses rod cells, which are more sensitive to faint light

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Binoculars are excellent for beginners — 10×50 is a recommended specification

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Always use a solar filter or projection method when observing the Sun; NEVER look directly at the Sun

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why should astronomers use red light at night? | Q: What is averted vision and why is it useful? | Q: What does 10×50 mean for binoculars?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Red light affects rod cells (responsible for night vision) less than white light, preserving dark adaptation. | Looking slightly to the side of a faint object uses the rod cells at the edge of the retina, which are more sensitive to dim light than the cone cells at the centre. | 10× magnification and 50mm objective lens diameter. The 50mm aperture determines light-gathering power.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Solar safety is CRITICAL — both boards emphasise this; NEVER look at the Sun without proper filtration 10×50 binoculars: 10× magnification, 50mm aperture — know this specification Averted vision uses rods — this is examined on both specifications Both AQA and Edexcel require practical observation as part of the course
